title: Slate: a documentation harness for work that keeps changing
summary: A portable harness that turns project notes into navigable, visual-first static docs, now powering this site's own documentation.

body.markdown: Documenting has become a constant need, so I collected all the learnings into a documentation harness. Slate is my answer to the recurring moment when a project outgrows scattered notes: the specs, plans, research, decisions and evidence are all useful, but only if they are easy to navigate later.

I wanted something I could drop into a repository, hand to an AI agent with raw material, and get back a static documentation site with structure, search, navigation and enough visual language to make dense work approachable. That made Slate less a single docs site and more a repeatable way to make docs sites.

The portfolio site has a lot of moving parts: a classic site, a 3D planet, content contracts, an editor, design systems and engineering rules. Every one of those areas needs a source of truth. A README was too flat, and a hand-built docs app would have become another product to maintain.

Slate keeps the boring parts generic. The package owns the reader shell, component vocabulary, runtime synchronization, schemas and validation scripts. The host owns its content, theme, manifest and meaning. That boundary means I can reuse the harness without mixing one project's decisions into another.

items.value: Project-agnostic documentation system and AI agent skill

body.markdown: At its simplest, Slate is a `slate/` folder a host can copy or vendor. The initializer creates the host's docs root, and the runtime tools keep generated shell files in sync so agents do not hand-edit the reader.

items.label: Static reader
items.text: The shell renders Markdown and HTML content through one sanitized pipeline with navigation, search, table of contents, theming and config-driven branding.

items.label: Visual-first authoring
items.text: The skill pushes structured content toward charts, SVG illustrations, figures, cards and comparisons before falling back to prose.

items.label: Host boundary
items.text: Generic runtime files stay in the package; the host keeps its own content, manifest, theme and authority rules.

items.label: Canvas view
items.text: For structured records, Slate Canvas adds a read-only React Flow surface with groups, repeated placements and named perspectives.

body.markdown: The real test is this site's documentation. It lives in the repository, is published as a Slate host, and stays close to the work it describes. A spec can link to a plan, a plan can link to validation evidence, and the reader can search across all of it without a server-side app.

That matters for agent work too. The docs are not just presentation; they are instructions, constraints and context. Slate makes that material readable for people while still being structured enough for an AI agent to follow.

The code is on GitHub at [prabinpebam/slate](https://github.com/prabinpebam/slate). A live example is this site's [Atiya documentation](https://prabinpebam.github.io/atiya/docs/), which is built from the repository's `documentation/` folder with the vendored Slate package.
